fixture.description: A synthetic `orders-service` repo with a base commit on `main` and a `feature/partial-refunds` branch. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` sits in the base commit of every variant so standards discovery is always exercised, and `specs/ORD-104-partial-refunds.md` is present in all variants but `defective-nospec`.

variants.defective: Ten planted defects, at least one per pyramid layer, deliberately crossing the severity/layer grain so that Supporting-layer findings are blocking and a Foundation-layer finding is not. Spec discoverable via `Closes ORD-104` in a commit message.
variants.defective-nospec: The same code, but no spec file ever existed and no commit message references a ticket. Tests whether the review caveats honestly rather than stalling or inventing conformance findings.
variants.regression: Reads clean on a diff review — every acceptance criterion implemented, tested, documented, SQL parameterized, naming and type hints conformant — but `post_refund` was rerouted to `refund`, which lacks the `already_refunded` guard that only `refund_order` still applies. A second full refund through the endpoint now returns a zero-cent refund where `main` rejected it, breaking AC-5. The suite passes; finding it takes executing both branches.
variants.clean: The same feature implemented correctly, including the guard the `regression` variant drops. No defects. Tests whether the review invents blocking findings when there are none.

fixture.placeholder: `<fixture-repo>` in each prompt below is the absolute path to the built fixture for that eval's variant.
fixture.notes: There is no CI in any variant. The suite runs locally via `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` and the README says so, which is what makes the skill's test-status rule testable: a review must establish status from the local run and say which signal it used, rather than reporting it unverified.
fixture.known_true_findings: Beyond the planted defects, three real issues exist in every variant and a correct review may raise any of them: `amount_cents` is never validated as an integer, so a float like 49.99 is accepted and stored; the check-then-act read of the refunded total has no transaction primitive; and in the `regression` and `clean` variants `refund_order` now delegates to `refund`, so the 90-day window applies to full refunds where it did not on `main`. Do not grade these as fabrications — they reproduce. The float gap in particular is the one unaided reviews catch and skill-driven ones have repeatedly missed, so it is worth tracking as a coverage signal.

evals.name: spec-present-defective-diff
evals.prompt: I've wrapped up the partial refunds work on this branch. Review the diff since main for me before I put it up for review. The repo is at <fixture-repo>.
evals.expected_output: Verdict is Request changes. The review finds the missing AC-4 refund window, the over-refund bug that ignores prior refunds, the f-string SQL injection, and the unrequested amount_cents -> amount rename, cites CODING_STANDARDS.md by rule where one is breached, quotes the spec line for each unmet requirement, separately flags the Slack notification as behavior the spec never asked for, and reports the committed skipped test and the missing AC-4 test as blocking. Findings are split by severity rather than by layer, each tagged with its pyramid layer and a file:line reference, under the skill's report template.
assertions: Verdict is 'Request changes'
Finds the missing 90-day refund window (AC-4 is not implemented at all) and quotes or cites the acceptance criterion
Finds the over-refund bug: the guard compares against the order total while ignoring refunds already recorded, so repeated partial refunds can exceed AC-2's limit
Finds the f-string SQL interpolation in _log_refund_audit and cites the CODING_STANDARDS.md database-access rule
Finds the amount_cents to amount rename in serialize_refund and identifies it as an unrequested breaking change to a client-facing contract
Flags the Slack notification separately as behavior the spec never asked for, rather than folding it into an unrelated finding
Reports the committed @pytest.mark.skip as a requested change, citing the standards rule that tests are never committed skipped
Notes that no test covers AC-4
Notes that README.md still documents amount_cents and the full-refund-only endpoint
Every finding carries a pyramid layer tag and a file or file:line reference
Report follows the template: verdict as an H2 heading on the first line, a summary paragraph, then 'Requested changes' and 'Suggestions', plus a 'Path to merge' sequence
Severity drives placement rather than layer: at least one Supporting-layer finding (documentation, tests, or style) appears under Requested changes
Every blocking finding reproduces when checked against the repo — no finding misstates what the code does
Every claim in the 'Checked and clean' section is true of the code; nothing is certified clean that a check would disprove
Every finding carries exactly one layer tag, and the tag matches the pyramid layer the finding actually belongs to rather than merely being present
Every acceptance criterion is accounted for explicitly in a 'Spec accounting' section rather than summarized in prose

evals.name: subtle-regression-diff
evals.prompt: Can you review this branch against main? I think it's ready to merge. The repo is at <fixture-repo>.
evals.expected_output: Verdict is Request changes, on the strength of the guard bypass. The review identifies that post_refund now routes through refund, which lacks the already_refunded guard, so a second full refund through the endpoint succeeds where main rejected it — an AC-5 regression the passing suite misses because its AC-5 test calls refund_order directly. Nothing that does not exist on this branch is reported.
